B: Hi! Hello, can you hear me?
A: Yes. Hi. Claire.
B: Gemma. Nice to meet you. Last one!
A: Yes.
B: Erm, so what do you do, Claire?
A: Dinner lady at a primary school in Ely. You?
B: I'm an upholsterer. Chairs, footstools, from a little unit in Didcot.
A: Oh. That's quite interesting, actually. Do you get old stuff, or people's IKEA sofas?
B: Mostly old stuff, thankfully. Nan's chairs, that kind of thing. I strip them back and sometimes there's horsehair, or newspaper from the fifties stuffed in for padding. I found a racing page from 1958 in one.
A: That's the best bit, I'd imagine. Like archaeology.
B: Exactly that! Archaeology with a staple gun. Sorry, I keep saying staple gun to people today.
A: It's fine. What fabrics do people want?
B: A lot of William Morris, actually. I love it, I've been to the V&A twice for the textiles.
A: I like Morris. I'm a bit sick of him on tea towels and phone cases, though. He'd have hated that, he was a socialist.
B: Ha, that's true, actually. Strawberry Thief on everything. Erm, I do sort of still love it, though.
A: No, the actual work's brilliant. It's the gift shop version I can't stand. I used to work in a gallery shop, so I've sold a lot of it.
B: Oh, did you? Were you an art person, then?
A: History of Art degree. I don't use it. Everyone asks.
B: I did a BTEC in art and design and then didn't do anything with it for about ten years. So I'm not asking. Upholstery was sort of how I found my way back.
A: That's quite a good way back, honestly. You actually make things.
B: Do you still draw, or anything?
A: A bit. Biro in notebooks. I don't show anyone.
B: Same, actually. Mine's mostly chair shapes and fabric ideas, nothing proper. I've never shown Rob.
A: Your husband's Rob? So's mine.
B: No! Oh my gosh, we've all got Robs. And I've got a greyhound, Pip.
A: We've got a greyhound. Moth.
B: Stop it. Does yours live on the sofa?
A: Permanently. And he won't go past the neighbour's cat.
B: Pip won't go out in the rain. Just stands at the door like, no.
A: That's very sensible of her, to be fair. Moth would walk to Cambridge if I let him, but only if there are no cats.
B: Ha. How old's your little one? I'm guessing there's a little one, with the fridge.
A: Alfie, nine. Minecraft, mainly.
